title: Image not showing for summary_large_image
description:
Hi! Many thanks for providing this package and your post about how to share presentations.

I am following the guide and I have problems with the [slides](https://user2021.llrs.dev) I'm working with at the moment. 
The twitter card validator doesn't find [the image](https://llrs.dev/2020/07/bioconductor-submissions-reviews/index_files/figure-html/first_plot-1.png) for the summary_large_image:
![Screenshot from 2021-06-05 16-42-30](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6818218/120895404-198db280-c61d-11eb-83e2-4c7f94ffdf5a.png)

Only when I changed to `twitter_card_type = "summary"` it did show the image. Is there something that images of the summary card should have?

I checked on the [help page](https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-for-websites/cards/overview/summary-card-with-large-image) but besides not having the ratio (it has ratio 1344/960) it meets the other requirements:

> Images for this Card support an aspect ratio of 2:1 with minimum dimensions of 300x157 or maximum of 4096x4096 pixels. Images must be less than 5MB in size. JPG, PNG, WEBP and GIF formats are supported. Only the first frame of an animated GIF will be used. SVG is not supported.

title: Cannot generate UTF-8 characters such as Chinese
description:
Hi,

It seems that the `meta` function is not able to properly generate UTF-8 characters on Windows.
Here is a minimally reproducible example:

````
---
title: "test"
date: "6/13/2020"
output: html_document
---

```{r open_graph_meta, include=FALSE}
# Add open graph meta information to the page.
library(metathis)
meta() %>%
  meta_description(
    "這裡") %>%
  meta_viewport() %>%
  meta_social(
    og_type="book",
    og_locale="zh_TW",
    twitter_card_type="summary"
  )
```
````

title: og tags need to use the property attribute
description:
Twitter `<meta>` tags use `name=`, OpenGraph uses `property=`.

```html
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary" />
<meta name="twitter:site" content="@nytimesbits" />
<meta name="twitter:creator" content="@nickbilton" />
<meta property="og:url" content="http://bits.blogs.nytimes.com/2011/12/08/a-twitter-for-my-sister/" />
<meta property="og:title" content="A Twitter for My Sister" />
```

title: Deploying on shinyapps.io when crawlers are blocked via robots.txt
description:
shinyapps.io uses a root-level, non-configurable `robots.txt` file to block all web crawlers. Any web crawlers that respect the [robots.txt specification](https://www.robotstxt.org/) will not show a preview for your app. This is why preview cards won't appear as expected on Twitter.

There are good reasons for this default behavior. Primarily, blocking web crawlers keeps ensures that your app isn't started up (incurring costs and hours against your quota) just to render the preview card. On the other hand, most social media sites implement some sort of caching mechanism.

At the moment, I am not aware of any way to configure the settings in the `robots.txt` file. It is served globally at the root level of `<user_name>.shinyapps.io`, so an app-specific `robots.txt` stored at `www/robots.txt` **won't have an effect or change the setting**.

I'll update this issue if these settings become configurable, or if anyone reports a work-around.
